speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and have they been getting worse steadily or in steps?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and the progression of walking, bladder, and speech issues over the last year, are your legs weak and stiff (spastic) or rather floppy and weak (flaccid), and do you have any numbness or tingling sensations?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (Shy-Drager Syndrome).

The combination of progressive gait difficulty, urinary incontinence, slurred speech, limb rigidity, tremor, and specifically orthostatic hypotension strongly suggests a parkinsonian disorder with autonomic failure. I have reached the limit of my questions and can proceed with this diagnosis.
